issue_request: FHIR-19714 was a Published FHIR-core change request resolved as Persuasive with Modification. It asked that the updates page clarify that although omitted elements in a PUT can empty previously stored data under normal replacement semantics, FHIR has no defined construct for explicitly setting an element empty in a PUT mode where omitted elements are typically retained.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites merge commit 0ff6d17906a8f3c24e9318d2063edcae8b3dd30d. The underlying implementation commit 0e62f8fbeddb2985a942147daf090ff72f4e21ab added the approved wording to source/updates.html, and follow-up commit e9fbfd39a29f11dcc4996bfae722b4b6fd85aeae removed an accidental duplicate sentence.
additional_context: source/updates.html is active in the current build/navigation via source/hierarchy.xml and source/implsupport-module.html. Later same-page work, including FHIR-32757 guidance and FHIR-44047 punctuation cleanup, did not alter or supersede the empty-element clarification. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no conflicting later decision or discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already preserves the approved sentence: HL7 v2-style retention of omitted elements can technically be followed in FHIR but is atypical and unexpected, and FHIR lacks a defined empty marker for PUT modes that retain omitted elements.
